title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 3 close: love infused from election — Augustine De grat. Christi 26
pass_a_gloss: No one would love God unless God infused charity into him; he would infuse saving charity into no one unless he had first destined him unto salvation. Therefore he does not destine eternal life to us from foresight of our love, but from the purpose of election unto eternal life he infuses this love into us. Let us conclude this our answer with the words of Augustine, who like a hammer everywhere bruises the Pelagians. Thus therefore he: That we might receive the love with which we should love, we were loved, when we did not yet have it. On the Grace of Christ against Pelagius, chapter 26.
pass_b_english: No one would love God unless God poured charity into him; God would pour saving charity into no one unless he had first destined him to salvation. So he does not destine eternal life from foresight of our love — from the purpose of election to eternal life he infuses that love. Close with Augustine, who hammers the Pelagians everywhere: "That we might receive the love with which we should love, we were loved when we did not yet have it" (On the Grace of Christ against Pelagius, ch. 26).
source_text: Nemo Deum diligeret, nisi Deus charitatem illi infunderet; nemini charitatem salutiferam infunderet, nisi eum prius ad salutem destinasset. Non ergo ex praevisione dilectionis nostrae destinat nobis vitam aeternam, sed ex proposito electionis ad vitam aeternam infundit nobis hanc dilectionem. Concludamus hoc responsum nostrum verbis Augustini, qui mallei instar ubique contundit Pelagianos. Sic ergo ille, Ut acciperemus dilectionem qua diligeremus, dilecti sumus, cum eam nondum haberemus. De grat. Christi contr. Pelag. cap. 26.
